findings.current: “No. Other than the fact that one of them is standing in front of me.”
findings.defect: The draft says Al Diab is standing, contradicting the established fact that he is seated.
findings.rationale: The Korean says only that one Muslim is before the narrator and does not change Al Diab’s seated position.
findings.replacement: “No. Other than the fact that one of them is sitting in front of me.”
findings.source: “모르지. 내 앞에 그중 한 명이 있다는 것 빼고는.”

findings.current: They abandoned the upper half of their bodies protected by the Fire Dragon Armor and targeted the exposed areas, including my lower body.
findings.defect: The syntax incorrectly makes the attackers abandon their own upper bodies, even though the armor protects the narrator and they are abandoning attempts to target his upper body.
findings.rationale: The source explains the attackers’ tactical adjustment: they stop attacking the armored upper body and redirect their attacks toward Taekyung’s exposed areas.
findings.replacement: They gave up on targeting my upper body, which was protected by the Fire Dragon Armor, and aimed for the exposed areas, including my lower body.
findings.source: 화룡갑에 의해 보호받는 상반신을 포기하고 하반신을 포함한 노출된 부위를 노린 것이다.

findings.defect: The Korean idiom means that the narrator finds the moment too irresistible to pass up, whereas the English ordinarily means he cannot tolerate it, reversing the punchline’s attitude.
findings.rationale: Taekyung prompted the Skeleton King to deliver the line and reacts with amused satisfaction, not distress or intolerance.

findings.current: The old man named Al Diab Jawahiri remained calm even as thunderous noises echoed outside and an unwelcome guest suddenly barged in.
findings.defect: The draft omits the narrator’s aside that Al Diab has a long name like other Arabs, losing a deliberate irreverent joke and part of Taekyung’s voice.
findings.rationale: 여느 아랍인처럼 긴 이름을 가진 explicitly characterizes the name as typically long and must not be omitted.
findings.replacement: The old man, whose name—Al Diab Jawahiri—was as long as any other Arab’s, remained calm even as thunderous noises echoed outside and an unwelcome guest suddenly barged in.
findings.source: 알 디아브 자와히리라는, 여느 아랍인처럼 긴 이름을 가진 노인은 밖에서 울려 퍼지는 굉음과 갑자기 들이닥친 불청객 앞에서도 침착했다.

findings.current: Nor did he care about the countless people who would suffer in the future.
findings.defect: The draft changes the governing idea from refusing to understand the future victims’ suffering to not caring about them.
findings.rationale: This fragment continues the preceding statement that Al Diab does not know or try to understand the suffering caused by his rhetoric; the source does not independently state that he does not care.
findings.replacement: Or how many countless people would suffer in the future.
findings.source: 그리고 앞으로 고통받을 무수한 이들에 관해서.

findings.current: An attack filled with the will to stake everything on it.
findings.defect: The established rendering of 일격 as “One Strike” is not used, and 필사의 의지 is expressed less naturally than the source’s desperate resolve.
findings.rationale: The binding terminology maps 일격 to “One Strike,” while 필사의 conveys resolve born of desperation or willingness to die.
findings.replacement: Their One Strike carried desperate resolve.

summary: The draft contains one scene-state contradiction, one misassigned physical action, a reversed closing punchline, and several localized fidelity or terminology issues.
